name: WCAG 2.1 Level AA (artefact-applicable subset)
source: W3C Web Content Accessibility Guidelines 2.1, Level AA conformance
applicabilityNote: Use when the artefact must support accessibility constraints. Subset filtered to checkpoints assessable from a text-based artefact (flow, IA, journey-map, etc.) — image-pixel-level WCAG criteria are out of scope.

heuristics.name: Text alternatives (1.1.1)
heuristics.description: All non-text content has a text alternative serving an equivalent purpose. For artefact-level audit: every interactive element in the flow/IA/matrix declares an accessible name.

heuristics.name: Info and relationships (1.3.1)
heuristics.description: Information, structure, and relationships conveyed visually are programmatically determinable. For artefact audit: relationships between elements (parent/child, before/after, group membership) are made explicit, not implied by visual position alone.

heuristics.name: Meaningful sequence (1.3.2)
heuristics.description: The reading and operation order is preserved regardless of presentation. For artefact audit: the flow / journey order is sequential and does not depend on visual layout.

heuristics.name: Keyboard (2.1.1)
heuristics.description: All functionality is operable through a keyboard interface. For artefact audit: every interactive step in the flow is reachable and triggerable from keyboard alone.

heuristics.name: No keyboard trap (2.1.2)
heuristics.description: Focus can be moved away from any component using only the keyboard. For artefact audit: modal/blocking steps in the flow include a documented exit path.

heuristics.name: Timing adjustable (2.2.1)
heuristics.description: Time limits set by the content are adjustable or can be turned off. For artefact audit: time-constrained steps (auto-logout, session timeout) include an extend/disable affordance.

heuristics.name: Labels or instructions (3.3.2)
heuristics.description: Labels or instructions are provided for user input. For artefact audit: every form/input element in the flow has a documented label and instruction.

heuristics.name: Error identification (3.3.1)
heuristics.description: Input errors are identified and described to the user in text. For artefact audit: error states in the flow are explicitly documented with the error message text.

heuristics.name: Error suggestion (3.3.3)
heuristics.description: Suggestions for correction are provided when an input error is detected. For artefact audit: error states include the correction path (not just the error name).

heuristics.name: Consistent navigation (3.2.3)
heuristics.description: Navigational mechanisms are presented in the same relative order each time. For artefact audit: IA navigation patterns are consistent across the structure.
